call_points.text: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 15% for FY27, in line with the Q1 print.
About USD20 million of Molycop synergies expected over the next two to two and a half years.
Molycop 10-month outlook: volume up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on a comparable basis.
Tega capex, including Chile, guided at about USD40 million for FY27.
Chile plant soft commissioning around January 2027, commercial production in March, subject to local approvals.
Tega consumable and equipment order book is ₹1,230 Cr, providing visibility for future revenue.
Cross-sell revenue between Tega and Molycop is expected to ramp only from Q3-Q4 of FY27.
Tega passes through raw material and freight cost increases with about a one-quarter lag, holding gross margin near 62%.
Molycop net debt is expected to fall between now and year-end; non-core land sale proceeds will repay debt.
Equipment revenue fell 44% on customer clearance delays; management gave no recovery timeline.
Consumable business expected to maintain normal CAGR of about 15% going forward.
Chile plant construction is on track for commissioning by early Q3.
Order book was ₹1,206 Cr at 31 March 2026, with ₹906 Cr executable within one year.

operating_notes.text: Crisil rated total bank loan facilities at ₹2,000 Cr, downgraded to Crisil A+/Stable and Crisil A1.

Board approved a facility agreement for a borrowing facility of up to ₹1,500 Cr from Standard Chartered Bank and other lenders, and an investment of up to USD 5 million in Tega MC Investment Pte. Ltd. via OCRPS, both to fund the proposed Mo

ICRA: order-to-cash cycles typically 6-9 months and receivable days 30-90 depending on customer and geography; average working capital utilisation ~31% of ₹221 Cr sanctioned limits in 12 months to March 2026.

ICRA: standalone capex of ₹220-230 Cr and repayments of ₹50-60 Cr over the next two years, met from operations; consolidated FY2027 internal accruals of ~₹900 Cr expected to cover capex and debt repayment.
Executed a rupee facility agreement of up to ₹1,500 Cr on May 22, 2026, to fund the Molycop acquisition.

Molycop has 13 grinding ball manufacturing facilities, 3 active joint ventures and 1 potential joint venture in progress, with a local presence in over 40 countries including USA, Canada, Mexico, Chile, Peru, Australia and Indonesia.

The acquisition was struck at an enterprise valuation of approximately USD 1.5 billion on a locked-box basis using Molycop's audited balance sheet as of June 30, 2025; the closing purchase price was USD 393 million with USD 18 million in es

Sellers are entitled to a contingent payment of up to USD 120 million within a maximum of 45 months if Molycop meets specified performance metrics, which may be funded from Molycop's internal accruals.
Molycop supplies grinding media and chemicals for SAG and ball mills, with a client network of 400+ mines in 40 countries and a history of over 100 years.
Combined Tega-Molycop group has 26 global manufacturing sites after adding Molycop's 13 facilities, 3 active JVs and 1 potential JV.
Tega's priority for the first 8 quarters after closing is operational and business integration.
Order book at 31 March 2026 was ₹1,206 Cr, of which ₹906 Cr is executable within one year.
FY26 one-time expenses of about ₹84 Cr covered labour-code impact and Molycop acquisition professional and consultancy charges.
Molycop acquisition completed on 1 June 2026 in partnership with Apollo Funds.
Molycop 12-month volume to June 2026 was 1.204 million tons versus 1.223 million tons a year earlier, with 12-month EBITDA up 11% to USD191 million.
Tega's gross margin excluding Molycop was about 62% versus 59% a year earlier; Molycop gross margin was about 36%.
About 85% of Molycop contracts are tied to steel indices, so revenue moves with steel prices while profit per ton is protected.

Calcutta High Court set aside Income Tax reassessment proceedings against Tega McNally Minerals for AY2017-18, voiding a demand of Rs 13,78,92,170 including interest; company reported no quantifiable financial impact.

timeline.summary: Shareholders re-appointed Mr. Jagdishwar Prasad Sinha (DIN: 02345086) as Independent Director via remote e-voting on April 18, 2026, with required majority.
On April 24, 2026, Tega Industries said CFO Sharad Kumar Khaitan would resign effective May 05, 2026, with GM-Finance Shyama Prasad Ganguly named Interim CFO from May 06, 2026.
Promoters Madan Mohan Mohanka, Manju Mohanka, Manish Mohanka, Mehul Mohanka, and related entities declared no encumbrances on Tega Industries shares as of March 31, 2026.
Tega Industries disclosed its Monitoring Agency report for Q4FY26, showing nil utilization of ₹1,713.29 Cr preferential issue proceeds.

On May 20, 2026, Tega Industries disclosed ICRA's assignment of [ICRA]A+/[ICRA]A1 to its ₹2,000 Cr bank facilities, all placed on Watch with Developing Implications pending completion of the Molycop acquisition.
Tega Industries executed a ₹1,500 Cr term loan facility agreement with Standard Chartered Bank and other lenders to fund the Molycop acquisition.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹526.78 Cr (-1.7% YoY), net profit ₹42.67 Cr (-58.1% YoY).

On June 1, 2026, Tega Industries completed the Molycop acquisition: its wholly owned Tega HoldCo acquired ~84.2% of Tega MC JV Holdings Pte. Ltd. for USD 394,295,423, with Apollo HoldCo taking ~15.8%, at an enterprise valuation of about USD 1.5 billion.

On June 1, 2026, Tega Industries completed the acquisition of Molycop in consortium with Apollo Funds at an enterprise value of approx. USD 1.5 billion, becoming its controlling shareholder with 13 plants added and 26 combined manufacturing sites.

On June 1, 2026, Tega Industries filed its FY26 investor presentation: total income ₹1,774 Cr (+5% YoY), adjusted PAT ₹227 Cr (+13%), reported PAT ₹143 Cr (-29%) after ₹84 Cr of one-time costs, and an order book of ₹1,206 Cr at 31 March 2026.
Tega Industries Limited uploaded the earnings call recording for Q4FY26 and FY26 on June 02, 2026, at its investor relations website.
Tega Industries reported FY26 total income of ₹1,773.6 Cr (+5% YoY) and completed the Molycop acquisition.

On 13 August 2026 Tega Industries held its Q1FY27 earnings call, its first quarter consolidating one month of Molycop, reporting group revenue of ₹1,720 Cr at a 15% adjusted EBITDA margin and guiding to about 15% consolidated margin for FY27.

On 16 October 2026 Tega Industries said the Calcutta High Court, by order dated 14 October 2026 with a rectification on 15 October 2026, set aside Income Tax reassessment proceedings against its wholly owned subsidiary Tega McNally Minerals for AY2017-18, voiding a demand of ₹13.79 Cr including interest.
